articles.title: झारखंड : वेदांता के ईएसएल प्लांट में गैस की चपेट में आने से दो की मौत, सोहन के परिवार को 60 लाख मुआवजा और नौकरी - Johar LIVE
articles.search_term: ("हीट एक्शन प्लान" OR "गर्मी से राहत" OR चेतावनी OR "रेड अलर्ट" OR "ऑरेंज अलर्ट" OR "येलो अलर्ट" OR एडवाइजरी OR "राहत सामग्री" OR "राहत शिविर" OR मुआवजा) Chhattisgarh
articles.full_text:
बोकारो : झारखंड के बोकारो जिले में वेदांता समूह की कंपनी ईएसएल स्टील लिमिटेड के प्लांट में गैस की चपेट में आने से दो कर्मचारियों की मौत हो गई. घटना 11 अक्टूबर 2026 को चंदनकियारी के सियालजोरी स्थित प्लांट के ब्लास्ट फर्नेस-1 में हुई. मृतकों की पहचान सोहन महतो और समीर अंसारी के रूप में हुई है. प्रारंभिक जांच में कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड गैस की चपेट में आने की आशंका जताई गई है.
सोहन महतो कंपनी में एग्जीक्यूटिव ऑफिसर के पद पर कार्यरत थे, जबकि समीर अंसारी कंपनी के एक बिजनेस पार्टनर के यहां इंजीनियर थे. घटना के बाद जिला प्रशासन और फैक्ट्री निरीक्षण विभाग ने जांच शुरू कर दी है. कंपनी ने भी घटना की स्वतंत्र जांच कराने और प्रभावित परिवारों को सहयोग देने की बात कही है.
घटना के बाद सोहन महतो के परिवार को 60 लाख रुपये मुआवजा देने और परिवार के एक सदस्य को नौकरी देने पर सहमति बनी है. इसमें अंतिम संस्कार के लिए तत्काल दो लाख रुपये दिए गए. शेष 58 लाख रुपये तीन महीने के भीतर परिवार के बैंक खाते में जमा किए जाने हैं.
समीर अंसारी के परिवार के लिए मुआवजे और नौकरी को लेकर उपलब्ध जानकारी में कोई स्पष्ट विवरण सामने नहीं आया है.
72 घंटे में जांच रिपोर्ट देने का निर्देश
बोकारो के उपायुक्त अजय नाथ झा के अनुसार, चास के अनुमंडल पदाधिकारी प्रांजल दंडा ने कार्यपालक दंडाधिकारी जया कुमारी और फैक्ट्री इंस्पेक्टर शिवानंद लागुरी को घटनास्थल का निरीक्षण कर 72 घंटे के भीतर विस्तृत रिपोर्ट सौंपने का निर्देश दिया है.
मुख्य कारखाना निरीक्षक मनीष कुमार सिन्हा ने प्रारंभिक तौर पर कार्बन मोनोऑक्साइड गैस की आशंका जताई है. हालांकि, हादसे की वास्तविक वजह जांच और पोस्टमार्टम रिपोर्ट के बाद स्पष्ट होगी.
वेदांता के प्लांट में पहले भी हो चुके हैं हादसे
इंडिया टुडे हिंदी के रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, वेदांता समूह की इकाइयों में इससे पहले भी जानलेवा औद्योगिक हादसे हो चुके हैं. 23 सितंबर 2009 को छत्तीसगढ़ के कोरबा स्थित बाल्को के कैप्टिव पावर प्लांट में निर्माणाधीन करीब 240 मीटर ऊंची चिमनी ढह गई थी. इस हादसे में 45 मजदूरों की मौत हुई थी और 50 से अधिक लोग घायल हुए थे.
28 सितंबर 2021 को बोकारो के इसी ईएसएल स्टील प्लांट में बंद ब्लास्ट फर्नेस की मरम्मत के दौरान ऊंचाई से गिरने के कारण तीन मजदूरों की मौत हुई थी. मृतकों की पहचान शाहनवाज आलम, मोहम्मद ओसामा और मोहम्मद सुल्तान के रूप में हुई थी.
14 अप्रैल 2026 को छत्तीसगढ़ के सक्ती जिले के सिंहितराई स्थित वेदांता पावर प्लांट में बॉयलर ट्यूब फटने से बड़ा हादसा हुआ था.
पत्रकार आनंद दत्त की 16 अप्रैल की रिपोर्ट में उस समय 17 मौतों का उल्लेख था. बाद में मृतकों की संख्या बढ़कर 25 हो गई.
सुरक्षा व्यवस्था पर फिर उठे सवाल
प्रकाशित रिपोर्ट में वेदांता की वित्त वर्ष 2020 की वार्षिक रिपोर्ट के आंकड़ों का हवाला देते हुए बताया गया था कि काम से जुड़े हादसों में कंपनी के सात कर्मचारियों की जान गई थी. रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, सुरक्षा से जुड़ी 70 प्रतिशत घटनाएं दोबारा हुई घटनाएं थीं और 90 प्रतिशत से अधिक घटनाओं का असर बिजनेस पार्टनर तथा ठेका कर्मचारियों पर पड़ा था.
बोकारो के ईएसएल प्लांट में दो कर्मचारियों की मौत के बाद एक बार फिर औद्योगिक इकाइयों में गैस सुरक्षा, कार्यस्थल पर निगरानी और कर्मचारियों की सुरक्षा व्यवस्था को लेकर सवाल खड़े हुए हैं. जांच रिपोर्ट से स्पष्ट होगा कि हादसा किन परिस्थितियों में हुआ और सुरक्षा व्यवस्था में कहीं चूक हुई थी या नहीं.

Bugatti’s 1,800-HP Tourbillon Shrugs Off Scorching Heat
Engineers push the Bugatti Tourbillon through Spain, Dubai, and Sweden to prove its cooling, climate control, and hybrid systems work in brutal conditions.
Bugatti has a new episode in its "A New Era" documentary series, and this one is about heat, not snow. The development team took the Tourbillon to Seville, where track and road temperatures climbed past 45°C (113°F), to see whether the hypercar's cooling systems could keep both the powertrain and the cabin under control.
The Tourbillon pairs a naturally aspirated V16 with three electric motors for a combined 1,800 horsepower. Two of the motors sit on the front axle, with a third backing up the V16 at the rear, and an 800V battery ties it all together. That architecture generates a thermal load Bugatti needed to prove it could manage without reshaping the car's bodywork.
Spain Testing Puts Cooling And Climate Control Under Pressure
Bugatti Tourbillon (2026) in southern Spain
Photo by: Bugatti
The Spanish test program followed earlier validation runs in Dubai and Sweden. Together they round out a climate trial meant to expose weaknesses before customer cars reach the road. More than 200 thermocouples were wired through the prototype to track how individual zones responded as the car moved between environments.
Daniel Ríos Hidalgo, a vehicle development engineer at BugattiRimac, said the goal was cooling the cabin and engine bay without compromising the car's shape. "In order not to compromise the shape and the design, we have very clever cooling circuits and cooling systems inside the car to make sure that all the systems remain under controlled temperatures," he said.
Paolo Magrone, a vehicle development driver at Bugatti Rimac, said performance came ahead of comfort for its own sake. "When you have a lot of power but you don't feel comfortable on the track or on the road, it's very difficult to be precise," he said, adding that keeping the cabin cool lets owners "enjoy the car at its best." The Tourbillon's interior was engineered with that same priority in mind, long before the Seville heat tested it.
Bugatti ran the car on both public roads and a racetrack to separate two different stresses. Open roads reached around 45°C (113°F), mimicking what an owner might face in a hot climate. The track piled on sustained loads across tires, brakes, powertrain and cooling systems all at once.
Gallery: Bugatti Tourbillon (2026) in Southern Spain
12
Source: Bugatti
Tourbillon Has Already Faced 122-Degree Heat And Bitter Cold
Spain wasn't the first extreme the Tourbillon has seen. About 15 months earlier, an XP prototype was pushed through Dubai heat exceeding 50°C (122°F), long before the more refined validation cars arrived in Seville for this latest round.
On the opposite end, Bugatti ran winter testing in Arjeplog, Sweden, where temperatures dropped to -30°C (-22°F). That program concentrated on low-grip handling, braking and stability systems, plus whether the cabin could stay livable in severe cold.

"We are delivering cars all over the world," Ríos Hidalgo said. "We have customers from lots of places that are going to drive the cars in different conditions. We need to make sure that these cars perform properly in all these varieties of conditions." Bugatti treats the hot and cold programs as complementary halves of the same validation effort, each confirming the car behaves consistently once simulation meets real pavement.
All 250 Tourbillon units are already sold, with deliveries beginning in 2026 and the final car expected to reach its owner by 2029. Bugatti plans to build roughly 80 cars a year at its La Manufacture facility in Molsheim, with pricing starting at €3.8 million ($4.26 million) before taxes.

Protect your spinach crops from extreme heat this summer
As extreme heat and drying weather hit South Africa, local spinach producers face severe crop wilting and disease risks. Farmers are fighting back by shifting watering schedules, applying mulch, and using shade netting
As South Africa experiences increasingly hot and dry conditions, local spinach farmers are adjusting daily field operations to safeguard their crops against severe heat stress, moisture loss and disease.
While conservation practices and microclimate management offer immediate relief on the ground, agricultural experts stress that long-term resilience will ultimately require substantial capital investment in irrigation infrastructure.
With atmospheric shifts and developing El Niño patterns bringing above-normal summer temperatures and severe heatwave risks across Southern Africa, these field-level pressures are intensifying. Meteorological forecasts indicate a drier, significantly hotter season, effectively turning climate adaptation from a future strategy into an urgent, daily operational reality for leafy vegetable growers.
Conservation farming and irrigation investments
Retaining soil moisture is a critical defence during high-temperature periods. Hamond Motsi, a PhD researcher at Stellenbosch University, notes that while organic soil management improves moisture retention, long-term water security requires dedicated infrastructure.
“The issue of water is a huge problem, particularly moisture. Conservation farming practices definitely help, but combining them with investment in irrigation is most important. Adding organic matter helps the soil retain available moisture and prevents rapid loss.
However, Motsi warned that soil management alone cannot offset severe dry spells, pointing to changing weather patterns in the Western Cape.
“In the long term, irrigation is going to be crucial. This year in the Western Cape was so dry it hardly rained or got cold. Farmers need to invest in irrigation as part of a long-term plan, but that requires major capital for dams, piping and associated technology,” he said.
On-the-ground impact: heat stress and disease
For vegetable producers, high daytime temperatures present immediate operational challenges. Extreme heat accelerates moisture loss and causes midday wilting, while stressed plants can become more vulnerable to disease.
Farmers in the Eastern Cape and Limpopo have reported powdery mildew developing on older leaves, particularly where airflow is poor.
Luyolo Mfenqa, a crop farmer in the Eastern Cape, observed that daytime heat takes a direct toll on crop health.
“The heat has just started here. Nighttime is better, but daytime heat causes the spinach to wilt severely. Powdery mildew starts on the older leaves and gradually spreads.”
To manage fungal outbreaks during heat spikes, Mfenqa applies a homemade foliar treatment before installing protective shade netting.
“When I noticed the mildew, I sprayed a mixture of bicarbonate of soda, dishwashing liquid and Epsom salt. It stopped the spread to other leaves. But as extreme heat continues, I’ve had to cover the plants with shade cloth to filter the heat,” Mfenqa said.

Delhi saw heavy rain and thunderstorms on Monday after the India Meteorological Department (IMD) declared a red alert for all 11 districts of the national capital, warning of moderate to heavy rainfall across the National Capital Region (NCR). Apart from the intense weather, flight operations at Delhi airport remained normal. Read on to know more.
IMD Issues Red Alert In Delhi Amid Heavy Rainfall
According to reports by India Today, a western disturbance has impacted weather conditions across northern India, bringing severe thunderstorms and rainfall to several parts of the region. The IMD’s red alert warned of thunderstorms, lightning, gusty winds reaching speeds of up to 60 kmph and heavy rainfall exceeding 15 mm per hour until 9 am.
An orange alert was also notified for Faridabad, Gurugram, Rohtak and Sonipat in Haryana, along with nine districts in Uttar Pradesh. These areas were warned of thunderstorms, lightning, winds gusting at 40–60 kmph and moderate to intense rainfall.
Despite the adverse weather conditions, Delhi Airport confirmed that flight operations were continuing normally. In a post on X, the airport said its ground teams were coordinating with all stakeholders to minimise disruptions and ensure a smooth journey for passengers. Travellers were urged to contact their respective airlines for the latest flight updates.
The rainfall brought some relief from the recent warm weather, with cloudy skies and showers causing temperatures to drop by 1–2 degrees Celsius. However, the intense spell also caused disruption across parts of the capital. Roads near Jhandewalan Temple in Karol Bagh were left waterlogged, while other parts of Delhi reported uprooted trees and flooding.
Waterlogging And Traffic Delays In Delhi
The weather department cautioned commuters about possible traffic delays, an increased risk of road accidents and water accumulation on roads and in low-lying areas following the downpour.
The IMD advised people to check traffic conditions before leaving home, follow official traffic advisories and avoid roads that are prone to waterlogging. Despite Monday’s rain, daytime temperatures in Delhi are expected to remain between 31 and 35 degrees Celsius over the next few days. According to the IMD’s seven-day forecast issued on Sunday evening, dry weather and partly cloudy skies are expected from Tuesday to Saturday.
Sudden unseasonal rain or weather shifts in Delhi are typically caused by the interaction of a passing Western Disturbance combined with local atmospheric changes or monsoon transition phases.
Is Delhi under red alert today?
Yes, IMD has issued a red alert due to heavy rainfall.
What is Delhi famous for?
Delhi is famous as the capital of India, its rich Mughal and colonial history, iconic architectural landmarks, vibrant street food, and bustling historic markets.
